faq.a: Add your target income and your annual business expenses, then divide by the share left after your tax set-aside. That gives the gross revenue you need. Divide that by your billable hours for the year (hours per week times weeks per year) to get the hourly rate.
faq.q: How is the hourly rate worked out?

faq.a: Because expenses and taxes come out of what you bill. A freelancer who wants $80,000 in the bank still has to bill enough to cover software, equipment, and taxes on top of that $80,000.
faq.q: Why is the rate higher than my target income divided by my hours?

faq.a: Not every working hour is billable. Admin, pitching, and learning take time too. The 80 percent rate shows what to charge if only 80 percent of your hours are paid, so unpaid time does not eat your income.
faq.q: What is the 80 percent billable rate?

faq.a: No. It is a planning percentage you choose. Real US freelancer tax depends on your total income, deductions, state, and self-employment tax, so check the current rules or a tax professional before relying on it.
faq.q: Does the tax set-aside cover my real tax bill?
